reviewType: INDEPENDENT-ADVERSARIAL — reviewer did not author the subject; posture was to reject
verdictStatement: The citation repair itself is CORRECT and I could not falsify any factual claim in versioning-policy.v9.json. The delta is exactly as declared, byte-verified; the additive-only exit-class rule V4 is genuinely unaffected across the v1.6->v1.14 span, established by my own measurement which was BROADER than the author's; status, seal and discharge discipline are intact; all seven named dependents exit 0. The single blocker is against check-versioning-v9.py, NOT against versioning-policy.v9.json: the checker independently re-measures the span into a `measured` dict and then fails to compare 76 of 102 declared evidence leaves against it, including roughly twenty mechanically-checkable values it has ALREADY COMPUTED. A falsified value in any of them exits 0 with the full green banner. versioning-policy.v9.json needs no byte change to clear this; the checker does.

blockers.notAgainst: versioning-policy.v9.json — no byte of the contract is wrong; every declaration I tested is TRUE
blockers.title: The successor's own evidence block is 75% unenforced: the checker measures correctly, then does not compare the declaration against its measurement.
blockers.measured: I falsified every leaf under successorRevision.d9CitationRepair.{substanceUnchangedEvidence, directionPreservation, siblingCitationAudit} one at a time (bools inverted, ints +7, strings replaced with 'ADVERSARIAL-FALSEHOOD', lists extended) and ran check-versioning-v9.py on each. 102 leaves probed: 26 ENFORCED (non-zero exit), 76 UNENFORCED (exit 0, full green PASS banner).
blockers.whyThisIsNotMerelyProse: About twenty of the 76 are mechanically verifiable and the checker already computes the correct value into its `measured` dict (check-versioning-v9.py lines ~203-230) and then never compares the artifact's declaration to it. This is a free comparison left on the table, not an unverifiable narrative.

worstCases.issue: The artifact's own recorded sha256 of the superseded span endpoint can be replaced with garbage and the checker exits 0. Same for headSha256. This is squarely the freeze §7.2 recording obligation — the recorded digest of the very artifacts the span measurement rests on is unenforced.
worstCases.note: The checker's own PINS constant IS enforced; the artifact's recorded digests are a separate, uncompared surface.

worstCases.issue: Can be flipped false->true — the artifact would then assert on its face that D9 DOES depend on VERSIONING, which is precisely the B-SCV2-06 circularity this entire dependency record exists to refute — and the checker exits 0. Its sibling d9CitesAnyVersioningPolicyArtifact IS gated, so the block is half-enforced and a reader cannot tell which half.
worstCases.checkerReferences: 0 occurrences of the identifier in check-versioning-v9.py

worstCases.issue: All 11 entries falsifiable. The checker computes measured['byteIdenticalRoots'] at line ~225 and never compares the declared list to it. (I verified the declared list is exactly correct: 11 claimed, 11 actual, zero set difference.)

The declared exit-class NAME lists are falsifiable. The checker compares only .identical/.removed/.added against its measurement, never the name lists — so the artifact could enumerate wrong class names beside a correctly-gated identical:true.

Computed as measured[...] and used for the checker's OWN finding at line ~530, but the artifact's declared values are never compared. reasonCodesByteIdentical can be set to false, 0, 999 or the string 'true' — all exit 0.
All falsifiable; fileResolves/anchorResolves have 0 references anywhere in the checker. The audit that discovered the two remaining stale citations is itself unverified by the instrument.

blockers.relationToLaw18: The author closed the freeze §6 law 18 integer class completely and I confirmed it: 52/52 integer leaves reject a float respelling and 52/52 reject a bool respelling, ALL by position — zero admitted, zero collateral. The checkerDisposition.integerTypeGuard claim is accurate and in fact under-claims (the guard covers all 52 integer leaves in the artifact, not merely the integers v9 adds). The defect is the SYMMETRIC and undisclosed case: closed BOOLEAN scalars the successor newly adds are respellable to any value, including the opposite truth value. 15 of 139 boolean leaves admit an integer respelling at exit 0, and every one of those 15 sits inside the new d9CitationRepair evidence block.
blockers.whyItMattersHere: This corpus has now produced three defects from 'two instruments wrong in the same direction read as agreement'. This is a fourth variant and arguably sharper: ONE instrument measures correctly and then declines to compare. The artifact's checkerDisposition invites the reader to treat the evidence block as instrument-backed ('demonstrated by the checker's own mutation selftest'), and the freeze record will carry this block forward as the standing justification for the eight-version span. A later editor could silently falsify it with every instrument green.
remedy: Compare the declared values against the already-computed `measured` dict for: exitClassSet.v16/.v114, byteIdenticalRootsV16ToV114, codeVocabulary.reasonCodesByteIdentical/.errorCodesByteIdentical/.remediesAdded/.remediesRemoved, directionPreservation.preservedByteIdentical, reVerifiedAtHead.d9CitesVersioningInItsDependencies, and measuredBetween.supersededCitationSha256/.headSha256 (against PINS).
Gate every asserted boolean with an exact `type(x) is bool` check, symmetric to the existing `type(x) is int` guard.
Add bool-respelling mutations to MUTATIONS. The current 36 include exactly 5 float respellings (verified) but not one boolean respelling, which is why the gap is invisible to --selftest.
Recompute siblingCitationAudit.entries[*].fileResolves/anchorResolves against disk rather than accepting the declaration.
blockers.doesNotAffect: The V4 conclusion. The checker enforces the substantive span invariants from its own measurement (lines ~519-533), so a falsified declaration cannot produce a wrong V4 verdict — only a wrong RECORD.
